meta.audience: The Lord, and then the reader
meta.location: The whole land of the Nephites, and the mountains
principles: A prophet asking for the lesser disaster

world_behind.title: Nephi uses the power of Helaman 10 immediately
world_behind.text: Verses 3 and 4 have him asking for a famine within a year of receiving the promise.

world_behind.title: He asks for the smaller destruction
world_behind.text: Verse 4 sets famine against the sword and gives the reason: hunger might turn them, and the sword will not.

world_behind.title: The famine falls on everyone
world_behind.text: Verse 6 says the whole earth was smitten, Lamanites as well as Nephites, with thousands dying in the more wicked parts.

world_behind.title: The people go through their leaders
world_behind.text: Verse 8 has them pleading with the chief judges to ask Nephi, and verse 9 has the judges doing it.

world_behind.title: The band is destroyed and then rebuilt
world_behind.text: Verse 10 says the Gadiantons had become extinct. Verse 26 has a new band searching out the same plans and taking the same name.

world_behind.title: The second band beats both nations
world_behind.text: Verse 32 says they defied the whole armies of the Nephites and of the Lamanites.

world_behind.title: The chapter ends in the middle of the cycle
world_behind.text: Verses 34 through 37 run remembrance, forgetting, growing iniquity, and ripening across four years.

words.text: Coarse cloth worn as a sign of mourning or repentance. The record uses the word four times and the King James Bible forty-six, including Nineveh in Jonah 3:5. Verse 9 makes it the sign Nephi looks for before praying again.
Calmed, satisfied. The word occurs once in the record and twice in the King James Bible. Nephi asks that the anger be appeased in the destruction that has already happened.
Treated at 1 Nephi 4:19, in the phrase "not a whit." The record uses it eight times. Verse 19 uses it to say Lehi was equal to his brother in righteousness, in the record's only note about him here.
Wide and violent destruction. The word occurs once in the record and once in the King James Bible, at Acts 8:3, of Saul and the church.
To challenge openly, daring an enemy to act. The word occurs once in the record and five times in the King James Bible, four of them of Goliath. Verse 32 has robbers defying two national armies.
To repair or correct. The word occurs once in the record and once in the King James Bible. Verse 36 uses it for a year in which nothing changed.

phrases.term: Rather let there be a famine in the land, to stir them up in remembrance of the Lord their God
phrases.text: A prophet asking for a disaster on purpose. He names the aim in the same sentence: remembrance, and perhaps repentance.

phrases.term: The work of destruction did cease by the sword but became sore by famine
phrases.text: Mormon's accounting of the trade. The dying continues, and the cause changes.

phrases.term: The whole earth was smitten, even among the Lamanites as well as among the Nephites
phrases.text: The famine does not sort by nation. It falls hardest in the more wicked parts of the land, on both sides of the border.

phrases.term: They began to remember the Lord their God; and they began to remember the words of Nephi
phrases.text: Two rememberings in one sentence. The second is what sends them to the judges in verse 8.

phrases.term: When Nephi saw that the people had repented and did humble themselves in sackcloth
phrases.text: He waits for evidence before praying. The request came in verse 8, and the prayer comes after he saw something.

phrases.term: They have concealed their secret plans in the earth
phrases.text: The detail that undoes the victory. The band is extinct and the documents are buried, and verse 26 has a new band digging them up.

phrases.term: Wilt thou turn away thine anger, and try again if they will serve thee?
phrases.text: The plainest sentence in the prayer. Nephi asks for another attempt without predicting the outcome.

phrases.term: Lehi, his brother, was not a whit behind him as to things pertaining to righteousness
phrases.text: The record's one line about Lehi in this chapter. It is placed right after the people begin esteeming Nephi as a great prophet.

phrases.term: They did search out all the secret plans of Gadianton; and thus they became robbers of Gadianton
phrases.text: How a destroyed movement returns. New men find the old plans and take the old name.

phrases.term: This great evil, which came unto the people because of their iniquity, did stir them up again in remembrance
phrases.text: The same mechanism as the famine, working a second time. Mormon marks it as coming from their own iniquity.

phrases.term: In the eighty and fourth year they did not mend their ways
phrases.text: A year summarized by what failed to happen. Verse 36 gives three years in three clauses, each worse than the last.

verses.label: v. 1–5
verses.title: The famine asked for
verses.text: Contentions grow into war throughout the land, carried on by the secret band, lasting two years. Nephi asks the Lord to spare the people the sword and send famine instead, to stir them to remembrance and perhaps repentance. It is done, and in the seventy-fourth year the killing by sword stops and the famine becomes severe.

verses.label: v. 6–9
verses.title: Hunger and the request
verses.text: The earth is dry and yields no grain, and thousands perish among Lamanites and Nephites in the more wicked parts. Seeing that they will die, the people remember God and remember Nephi's words, and plead with their chief judges to ask him to pray. The judges do, and Nephi, seeing repentance and sackcloth, prays again.

verses.label: v. 10–16
verses.title: The second prayer
verses.text: He reports that the people have repented, swept away the band of Gadianton until it is extinct, and buried its plans. He asks that the anger be appeased in the destruction already done, that the famine cease, and that rain come so the earth brings forth grain. He recalls that the first prayer was answered and that God said he would spare a repentant people, and asks him to try again if they will serve him.

verses.label: v. 17–21
verses.title: Rain and recovery
verses.text: In the seventy-sixth year the anger turns away, rain falls, and the land yields fruit and grain. The people rejoice, stop seeking Nephi's life, and esteem him a great prophet, and Lehi is named as equal to him in righteousness. They prosper, rebuild the waste places, and spread from sea to sea. Two years pass in peace, with most Nephites and Lamanites in the church.

verses.label: v. 22–23
verses.title: Doctrinal strife
verses.text: A few contentions arise over points of doctrine laid down by the prophets, and in the seventy-ninth year much strife. Nephi, Lehi, and many who knew the true points, having revelations daily, preach until the strife ends that same year.

verses.label: v. 24–33
verses.title: The band returns
verses.text: In the eightieth year Nephite dissenters living as Lamanites, with some Lamanites they had stirred up, begin a war of murder and plunder, retreating into mountains and secret places and gaining recruits daily. They find the old plans and become robbers of Gadianton, doing great havoc among both peoples. Armies sent into the mountains are driven back twice, and the robbers grow strong enough to defy both nations, killing many and carrying away women and children.

verses.label: v. 34–38
verses.title: The cycle turns again
verses.text: The evil stirs the people to remembrance in the eighty-first year. In the eighty-second they begin to forget, in the eighty-third they wax strong in iniquity, in the eighty-fourth they do not mend their ways, and in the eighty-fifth they grow stronger in pride and wickedness, ripening again for destruction.

chapter.title: A prophet chooses the milder catastrophe
chapter.text: Verse 4 asks for famine in place of the sword because famine might produce remembrance. The reasoning is stated openly.

chapter.title: The power granted in Helaman 10 is used within a year
chapter.text: Verses 5 and 17 both say it was done according to his words, in opposite directions.

chapter.title: Repentance under compulsion still counts here
chapter.text: Verse 15 says they repented because of the famine, and the rain comes anyway. Alma 32:14 had ranked that kind of humility lower without calling it worthless.

chapter.title: The victory over the band is undone by a document
chapter.text: Verse 10 has the plans concealed in the earth, and verse 26 has them searched out. Destroying the members left the method intact.

chapter.title: The second band is stronger than the first
chapter.text: Verse 32 has it defying two national armies, where the first was destroyed by the Lamanites in Helaman 6:37.

chapter.title: Doctrinal strife is settled by preaching
chapter.text: Verse 23 has men with daily revelations ending it within the year. The record treats disputed doctrine as a teaching problem.

chapter.title: Four years are summarized in four clauses
chapter.text: Verses 36 and 37 compress forgetting, iniquity, unchanged ways, and pride into two verses. The pace itself makes the point.

chapter.title: The chapter is one full turn of the cycle
chapter.text: War, famine, repentance, prosperity, peace, forgetting, and ripening, inside thirty-eight verses. Helaman 12 will step back and comment on it.

applications.title: Ask for the smaller loss
applications.text: Nephi requested famine over the sword because one leaves people alive to change. When something has to give, choose the version that keeps a future open.

applications.title: Wait for evidence before you act on a request
applications.text: The judges asked, and Nephi looked for repentance first. Someone asking for relief is not yet a reason to give it.

applications.title: Destroy the method, not just the members
applications.text: The plans were buried and dug up again. Removing the people who ran something leaves the thing itself available.

applications.title: Notice the year nothing changed
applications.text: "They did not mend their ways" is a whole year. Stretches with no movement are worth naming as what they are.

questions.text: What would I ask for if the alternative were worse?
What did it take to make me remember last time?
Whose request am I acting on without looking first?
What have I buried rather than destroyed?
What would I want God to try again with me?
Whose steady equal work near me has gone unmentioned?
What have I not mended this year?
